ALL-IN-ONE WEDDING PLANNER
Setup Guide for Google Sheets and Excel

Thank you for your purchase. This planner is one file, Wedding-Planner-All-In-One.xlsx,
with 33 tabs covering every part of wedding planning: budget, guest list, seating,
checklist, vendors, and more. Everything updates automatically as you fill it in.


1. HOW TO OPEN THE FILE

Google Sheets (recommended for sharing with your partner or planner):
  1. Go to sheets.google.com and sign in.
  2. Click the folder icon (Open file picker) then the Upload tab.
  3. Upload Wedding-Planner-All-In-One.xlsx.
  4. Google Sheets will open it automatically. To keep it fully editable and make sure
     charts and formulas behave the same as Excel, click File > Save as Google Sheets.
     Work in that converted copy going forward.

Microsoft Excel:
  1. Double-click Wedding-Planner-All-In-One.xlsx to open it in Excel (2016 or later,
     or Microsoft 365).
  2. If you see a yellow "Enable Editing" bar at the top, click it.
  3. Save a personal working copy right away (File > Save As) so the original stays
     as a backup.

Both platforms open the file cleanly with no broken links. If any single cell ever
shows an error after you edit a formula cell by mistake, use Undo (Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z)
to revert it.


2. GETTING STARTED

  1. Open the "Get Started" tab first. Fill in your names, wedding date, and hashtag
     in the highlighted cells near the top. Many tabs (Dashboard, Checklist, Smart
     Calendar, Guest List) calculate dates and countdowns from this wedding date, so
     enter it first.
  2. Use the table of contents on the Get Started tab to jump to any of the 33 tabs.
  3. Visit the Dashboard tab any time for a full snapshot: budget, guest counts,
     checklist progress, and more, all pulled in automatically.
  4. Work through the Wedding Checklist tab, organized into 12 timeframes from
     12+ months out through the day before the wedding, plus a Legal Items section.
  5. Add your vendors on the Vendor Selection tab. Mark a vendor "Final: Yes" and
     enter the Amount, and it automatically fills in the Actual column on your
     Wedding Budget tab. No manual copying between tabs.
  6. Add guests on the Guest List tab. RSVP status and meal preference flow
     automatically into the Dashboard charts and into both Seating Plan tabs.


3. HOW THE AUTOMATION WORKS

  - Dashboard: every number and chart pulls live from other tabs with formulas
    (SUMIFS, COUNTIFS). You never enter numbers directly on the Dashboard.
  - Budget: the Actual column in the Expense Summary looks up the Vendor Selection
    tab automatically for any vendor marked Final.
  - Guest List and Seating: RSVP and meal preference answers on the Guest List
    feed the charts on that tab and the guest counts on both Seating Plan tabs.
  - Smart Calendar: pulls due dates from the Checklist and payment due dates from
    the Budget automatically. Choose a month and year at the top, and toggle the
    Budget, Checklist, Important Dates, Stationery, and Dance Lessons filters
    on or off with the checkboxes.
  - Checkboxes: cells that look like checkboxes (a checked or empty box) are TRUE/
    FALSE cells with a dropdown. Click the cell and choose from the dropdown, or in
    Google Sheets you can select the cell and press Ctrl+Enter for a shortcut toggle
    once you have used the dropdown once.


4. CUSTOMIZING COLORS AND NAMES

  - Names, wedding date, and hashtag: edit only the highlighted cells on the
    Get Started tab (A4, B4, C4, D4). Everything else updates on its own.
  - Dropdown lists (categories, statuses, meal choices, etc.): open the hidden
    "Lists" tab to edit any dropdown's options in one place.
      Google Sheets: right-click any sheet tab, choose "Show all sheets" or use
      Data > Named ranges to view Lists, then right-click the Lists tab and
      choose Unhide sheet if it does not show automatically.
      Excel: right-click any sheet tab, choose Unhide, and select Lists.
    Edit the values in that column and every dropdown using it updates instantly.
    When you are done, you can hide the tab again (right-click > Hide sheet), it
    is just kept out of the way, not locked.
  - Colors: each tab uses a soft pastel theme. To recolor a section, select the
    banner or table header cells and use the fill color tool. Formulas and
    formatting elsewhere are not affected by recoloring.
  - Charts: click any chart, then use your program's chart editor to adjust
    colors, labels, or size. The underlying data table for each chart sits in
    the columns just to the right of or below the chart, so you can see exactly
    what feeds it.


5. TIPS

  - Guest List and Gifts and Thank You are pre-built with 200 rows. If you need
    more, select the last formatted row, copy it, and paste into the new rows
    below to carry the formatting and dropdowns down.
  - The Wedding Checklist due dates are examples that pace out automatically
    from your wedding date. Adjust any individual due date at any time; it will
    not reset.
  - If a formula cell ever shows an error, it almost always means a referenced
    cell above it in that column was deleted rather than cleared. Undo, or copy
    the formula down again from a working row.
  - Save frequently, and keep a backup copy of the original file in case you want
    to start over.

Enjoy your planning, and congratulations on your wedding.
